FastAPI — Complete Engineering Reference

Scope: FastAPI fundamentals, path/query/body params, Pydantic models, dependency injection, routers, middleware, CORS, authentication (OAuth2, JWT), SQLAlchemy integration, async/await, background tasks, WebSockets, file uploads, testing (pytest + TestClient), rate limiting, caching (Redis), pagination, API versioning, health checks, observability (logging, OpenTelemetry), streaming responses (SSE for LLM serving), deployment (Docker, Gunicorn, Uvicorn), production best practices, interview Q&A.

•

1. FastAPI Fundamentals

FastAPI is a modern, high-performance Python web framework built on Starlette (ASGI) and Pydantic, providing automatic request validation, serialization, and interactive OpenAPI documentation from standard Python type hints. Its async-native design and built-in dependency injection make it the go-to choice for building production-grade APIs and ML model serving endpoints.

from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI(
    title="My API",
    description="Production-grade API",
    version="1.0.0",
)

@app.get("/")
async def root():
    return {"message": "Hello, World!"}

# Run: uvicorn main:app --reload
# Docs: http://localhost:8000/docs (Swagger UI)
# Alt docs: http://localhost:8000/redoc
WHY FASTAPI?
  - Fastest Python web framework (Starlette + Pydantic)
  - Automatic OpenAPI/Swagger docs
  - Type hints → auto validation + serialization
  - Async-native (ASGI)
  - Dependency injection built-in
  - Production-ready with proper deployment
•

2. Path, Query & Body Parameters

FastAPI automatically extracts and validates path, query, and body parameters from incoming requests using Python type annotations and Pydantic models. Path parameters are part of the URL, query parameters are appended after ?, and body parameters are sent as JSON — each with built-in constraints like ge, min_length, and required/optional semantics.

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, Path, Body
from typing import Optional

# ── Path parameters ──────────────────────────────────────
@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
async def get_item(
    item_id: int = Path(..., title="The ID of the item", ge=1)
):
    return {"item_id": item_id}

# ── Query parameters ────────────────────────────────────
@app.get("/items/")
async def list_items(
    skip: int = Query(0, ge=0),
    limit: int = Query(10, ge=1, le=100),
    q: Optional[str] = Query(None, min_length=1, max_length=50),
):
    return {"skip": skip, "limit": limit, "q": q}

# ── Body parameters (JSON) ──────────────────────────────
from pydantic import BaseModel

class ItemCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float
    description: Optional[str] = None

@app.post("/items/")
async def create_item(item: ItemCreate):
    return item
•

3. Pydantic Models & Validation

Pydantic models define the shape, types, and validation rules for request and response data using Python dataclass-like syntax with runtime enforcement. Field-level validators, model-level cross-field checks, and JSON schema generation ensure that invalid data is rejected before it reaches your business logic.

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator, model_validator
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum

class Priority(str, Enum):
    low = "low"
    medium = "medium"
    high = "high"

class TaskCreate(BaseModel):
    title: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=200)
    description: str = Field(default="", max_length=1000)
    priority: Priority = Priority.medium
    due_date: Optional[datetime] = None
    tags: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=10)
    
    @field_validator("tags")
    @classmethod
    def validate_tags(cls, v):
        return [tag.lower().strip() for tag in v]
    
    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_due_date(self):
        if self.due_date and self.due_date < datetime.now():
            raise ValueError("Due date must be in the future")
        return self

    model_config = {"json_schema_extra": {
        "examples": [{"title": "Buy groceries", "priority": "high"}]
    }}
•

4. Response Models & Status Codes

Response models control exactly which fields are returned to the client and how they are serialized, while explicit status codes communicate the outcome of each operation. Using response_model with Pydantic ensures consistent, documented API responses and prevents accidental leakage of internal fields.

from fastapi import status

class TaskResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    title: str
    priority: Priority
    created_at: datetime

    model_config = {"from_attributes": True}  # ORM mode

@app.post(
    "/tasks/",
    response_model=TaskResponse,
    status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    summary="Create a new task",
    response_description="The created task",
)
async def create_task(task: TaskCreate):
    # ... create in DB
    return task_db

# ── Multiple response types ─────────────────────────────
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

@app.get("/tasks/{task_id}", responses={
    200: {"model": TaskResponse},
    404: {"description": "Task not found"},
})
async def get_task(task_id: int):
    task = db.get(task_id)
    if not task:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Task not found")
    return task
•

5. Dependency Injection

FastAPI's dependency injection system lets you declare reusable, composable functions or classes that are automatically resolved and injected into endpoint handlers via Depends(). This pattern cleanly separates cross-cutting concerns — database sessions, authentication, pagination — making code modular, testable, and easy to override in tests.

from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException

# ── Simple dependency ────────────────────────────────────
async def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db  # Generator-based (handles cleanup)
    finally:
        db.close()

@app.get("/items/")
async def list_items(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return db.query(Item).all()

# ── Auth dependency ──────────────────────────────────────
async def get_current_user(token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme)):
    user = decode_token(token)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid token")
    return user

@app.get("/me")
async def read_me(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
    return user

# ── Class-based dependency ───────────────────────────────
class Pagination:
    def __init__(self, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 10):
        self.skip = skip
        self.limit = limit

@app.get("/items/")
async def list_items(pagination: Pagination = Depends()):
    return db.query(Item).offset(pagination.skip).limit(pagination.limit).all()
•

6. Routers & Project Structure

Routers (APIRouter) let you split a FastAPI application into modular, independently testable files organized by domain, while a well-defined project structure separates models, schemas, services, routers, and configuration. This organization is essential for maintainability as applications grow beyond a single-file prototype.

PROJECT STRUCTURE:
  app/
  ├── main.py              # FastAPI app, startup events
  ├── config.py             # Settings (pydantic-settings)
  ├── database.py           # DB engine, session
  ├── models/               # SQLAlchemy models
  │   ├── user.py
  │   └── task.py
  ├── schemas/              # Pydantic schemas
  │   ├── user.py
  │   └── task.py
  ├── routers/              # API routers
  │   ├── users.py
  │   └── tasks.py
  ├── services/             # Business logic
  │   └── task_service.py
  ├── dependencies.py       # Shared dependencies
  └── tests/
      └── test_tasks.py
# routers/tasks.py
from fastapi import APIRouter

router = APIRouter(prefix="/tasks", tags=["tasks"])

@router.get("/")
async def list_tasks(): ...

@router.post("/")
async def create_task(): ...

# main.py
from app.routers import tasks, users
app.include_router(tasks.router)
app.include_router(users.router)
•

7. Middleware & CORS

Middleware intercepts every request and response to perform cross-cutting tasks like logging, timing, and header injection, while CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) middleware controls which external domains can call your API. Correctly configuring CORS is critical for browser-based clients, and custom middleware provides a single place for request-level observability.

from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
import time, logging

# ── CORS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["https://mysite.com"],  # Never use ["*"] in production
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

# ── Custom middleware (logging + timing) ─────────────────
class RequestLoggingMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request, call_next):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        response = await call_next(request)
        duration = time.perf_counter() - start
        logging.info(f"{request.method} {request.url.path} → {response.status_code} ({duration:.3f}s)")
        response.headers["X-Process-Time"] = str(duration)
        return response

app.add_middleware(RequestLoggingMiddleware)
•

8. Authentication (OAuth2, JWT)

FastAPI provides built-in OAuth2 support with automatic Swagger UI integration for token-based authentication using JWTs (JSON Web Tokens). The typical flow — credentials → JWT issuance → bearer token validation via a dependency — secures endpoints while keeping authentication logic cleanly separated from business logic.

from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer, OAuth2PasswordRequestForm
from jose import jwt, JWTError
from passlib.context import CryptContext
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

SECRET_KEY = "your-secret-key"
ALGORITHM = "HS256"

pwd_context = CryptContext(schemes=["bcrypt"])
oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="token")

def create_token(data: dict, expires_delta: timedelta = timedelta(hours=1)):
    to_encode = data.copy()
    to_encode["exp"] = datetime.utcnow() + expires_delta
    return jwt.encode(to_encode, SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM)

async def get_current_user(token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme)):
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM])
        username = payload.get("sub")
        if not username:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid token")
    except JWTError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid token")
    user = get_user(username)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="User not found")
    return user

@app.post("/token")
async def login(form_data: OAuth2PasswordRequestForm = Depends()):
    user = authenticate_user(form_data.username, form_data.password)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Incorrect credentials")
    token = create_token({"sub": user.username})
    return {"access_token": token, "token_type": "bearer"}
JWT (JSON WEB TOKEN) — HOW IT WORKS:

  A JWT is a compact, URL-safe token format for securely transmitting
  claims between parties. It consists of three Base64-encoded parts
  separated by dots:

  HEADER.PAYLOAD.SIGNATURE
  
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 1. HEADER (algorithm + type)                                   │
  │    {"alg": "HS256", "typ": "JWT"}                              │
  │                                                                │
  │ 2. PAYLOAD (claims — the data)                                 │
  │    {                                                           │
  │      "sub": "user123",        ← Subject (user ID)              │
  │      "exp": 1717000000,       ← Expiration (Unix timestamp)    │
  │      "iat": 1716996400,       ← Issued At                      │
  │      "role": "admin"          ← Custom claim                   │
  │    }                                                           │
  │                                                                │
  │ 3. SIGNATURE (integrity check)                                 │
  │    HMAC-SHA256(                                                │
  │      base64(header) + "." + base64(payload),                   │
  │      SECRET_KEY                                                │
  │    )                                                           │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  FLOW:
    1. Client sends credentials (username + password) to /token
    2. Server validates credentials against database
    3. Server creates a JWT with user info + expiration
    4. Server signs the JWT with SECRET_KEY and returns it
    5. Client stores the JWT (localStorage, cookie, memory)
    6. Client sends JWT in Authorization header: "Bearer <token>"
    7. Server decodes + verifies signature on every request
    8. If valid and not expired → grant access
    9. If invalid/expired → 401 Unauthorized

  KEY POINTS:
    • JWTs are SIGNED, not encrypted (payload is readable!)
    • Never store secrets in the payload
    • Use HTTPS to prevent token interception
    • Set short expiration (15-60 min) + refresh tokens
    • HS256 (symmetric) for single server, RS256 (asymmetric) for microservices
    • Revocation is hard — use token blacklists or short-lived tokens

COMMON HTTP STATUS CODES — COMPLETE REFERENCE:

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 1xx — INFORMATIONAL (request received, processing)             │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 100 Continue         — Server received headers, send body      │
  │ 101 Switching Proto  — Upgrading to WebSocket                  │
  │ 102 Processing       — Server is processing (WebDAV)           │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 2xx — SUCCESS                                                  │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 200 OK               — Standard success (GET, PUT, PATCH)      │
  │ 201 Created          — Resource created (POST)                 │
  │ 202 Accepted         — Request accepted, processing async      │
  │ 204 No Content       — Success, no body returned (DELETE)      │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 3xx — REDIRECTION                                              │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 301 Moved Permanently — Resource URL changed permanently       │
  │ 302 Found            — Temporary redirect                      │
  │ 304 Not Modified     — Use cached version (conditional GET)    │
  │ 307 Temporary Redirect — Same method redirect (POST stays POST)│
  │ 308 Permanent Redirect — Like 301 but preserves method         │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 4xx — CLIENT ERROR                                             │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 400 Bad Request      — Invalid syntax, malformed JSON          │
  │ 401 Unauthorized     — Authentication required / invalid       │
  │ 403 Forbidden        — Authenticated but no permission         │
  │ 404 Not Found        — Resource does not exist                 │
  │ 405 Method Not Allowed — Wrong HTTP method for this endpoint   │
  │ 408 Request Timeout  — Server timed out waiting for request    │
  │ 409 Conflict         — Conflict with current resource state    │
  │ 410 Gone             — Resource permanently deleted            │
  │ 413 Payload Too Large — Request body exceeds server limit      │
  │ 415 Unsupported Media — Wrong Content-Type                     │
  │ 422 Unprocessable    — Valid JSON but validation failed        │
  │                        ↑ FastAPI's default validation error    │
  │ 429 Too Many Requests — Rate limit exceeded                    │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ 5xx — SERVER ERROR                                             │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 500 Internal Server Error — Unhandled exception                │
  │ 502 Bad Gateway      — Upstream server returned invalid resp   │
  │ 503 Service Unavailable — Server overloaded or in maintenance  │
  │ 504 Gateway Timeout  — Upstream server didn't respond in time  │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  FastAPI COMMON MAPPINGS:
    GET    success → 200       POST   success → 201
    PUT    success → 200       DELETE success → 204
    Validation error → 422     Auth failure → 401
    Permission denied → 403    Not found → 404
    Rate limited → 429         Server bug → 500

  FastAPI USAGE:
    from fastapi import status
    
    @app.post("/items", status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
    @app.delete("/items/{id}", status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)
    raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Not found")
    raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail="Rate limit exceeded")
•

9. Database (SQLAlchemy)

SQLAlchemy integration gives FastAPI applications a full-featured ORM for defining database models, managing sessions, and running queries against relational databases. Using FastAPI's dependency injection to provide database sessions — with both synchronous and async engine support — ensures proper connection lifecycle management and clean separation of data access.

from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Column, Integer, String, DateTime
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

DATABASE_URL = "postgresql://user:pass@localhost/db"
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
Base = declarative_base()

class TaskModel(Base):
    __tablename__ = "tasks"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    title = Column(String(200), nullable=False)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

# ── Async SQLAlchemy ─────────────────────────────────────
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine, AsyncSession

async_engine = create_async_engine("postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@localhost/db")
AsyncSessionLocal = sessionmaker(async_engine, class_=AsyncSession)

async def get_async_db():
    async with AsyncSessionLocal() as session:
        yield session
•

10. Async, Background Tasks & WebSockets

FastAPI's async-native ASGI foundation supports async/await endpoints, background tasks that run after the response is sent, and persistent WebSocket connections for real-time bidirectional communication. Server-Sent Events (SSE) via StreamingResponse are particularly important for streaming LLM outputs token-by-token to clients.

from fastapi import BackgroundTasks, WebSocket

# ── Background tasks ────────────────────────────────────
def send_email(to: str, subject: str):
    # Long-running operation
    pass

@app.post("/notify/")
async def notify(bg: BackgroundTasks):
    bg.add_task(send_email, "user@example.com", "Hello")
    return {"message": "Notification queued"}

# ── WebSocket ────────────────────────────────────────────
@app.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    while True:
        data = await websocket.receive_text()
        await websocket.send_text(f"Echo: {data}")

# ── SSE (Server-Sent Events) for LLM streaming ──────────
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

async def generate_stream(prompt: str):
    async for chunk in llm.astream(prompt):
        yield f"data: {chunk.content}\n\n"
    yield "data: [DONE]\n\n"

@app.post("/chat/stream")
async def chat_stream(prompt: str):
    return StreamingResponse(
        generate_stream(prompt),
        media_type="text/event-stream"
    )
•

11. File Uploads & Streaming

FastAPI handles file uploads via UploadFile objects that provide async read access, filename metadata, and support for both small in-memory files and large files streamed to disk in chunks. This makes it straightforward to build endpoints for single, multiple, or large-file uploads with proper memory management.

from fastapi import UploadFile, File

@app.post("/upload/")
async def upload_file(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
    contents = await file.read()
    return {"filename": file.filename, "size": len(contents)}

# ── Multiple files ───────────────────────────────────────
@app.post("/upload-multiple/")
async def upload_multiple(files: list[UploadFile] = File(...)):
    return [{"filename": f.filename} for f in files]

# ── Large file (stream to disk) ─────────────────────────
@app.post("/upload-large/")
async def upload_large(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
    with open(f"uploads/{file.filename}", "wb") as f:
        while chunk := await file.read(1024 * 1024):  # 1MB chunks
            f.write(chunk)
    return {"filename": file.filename}
•

12. Rate Limiting & Caching

Rate limiting protects your API from abuse by restricting the number of requests per client per time window, while caching (typically with Redis) avoids recomputing expensive results for repeated queries. Together, they are essential for controlling cost, ensuring fair usage, and maintaining responsiveness under load.

# ── Rate limiting (slowapi) ─────────────────────────────
from slowapi import Limiter, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler
from slowapi.util import get_remote_address

limiter = Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address)
app.state.limiter = limiter
app.add_exception_handler(429, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler)

@app.get("/api/data")
@limiter.limit("10/minute")
async def get_data(request: Request):
    return {"data": "..."}

# ── Redis caching ────────────────────────────────────────
import redis.asyncio as redis
import json

redis_client = redis.from_url("redis://localhost:6379")

@app.get("/expensive/{item_id}")
async def get_expensive(item_id: int):
    cache_key = f"item:{item_id}"
    cached = await redis_client.get(cache_key)
    if cached:
        return json.loads(cached)
    
    result = expensive_computation(item_id)
    await redis_client.set(cache_key, json.dumps(result), ex=3600)  # TTL 1 hour
    return result
•

13. Pagination & API Versioning

Pagination returns large result sets in manageable pages using cursor-based or offset-based strategies, while API versioning (via URL prefixes or headers) lets you evolve your API without breaking existing clients. Cursor-based pagination is preferred for large datasets because it avoids the performance pitfalls of high offsets.

# ── Cursor-based pagination ──────────────────────────────
@app.get("/items/")
async def list_items(cursor: Optional[int] = None, limit: int = 20):
    query = db.query(Item).order_by(Item.id)
    if cursor:
        query = query.filter(Item.id > cursor)
    items = query.limit(limit + 1).all()
    
    has_next = len(items) > limit
    items = items[:limit]
    next_cursor = items[-1].id if has_next else None
    
    return {"items": items, "next_cursor": next_cursor}

# ── API versioning (router prefix) ──────────────────────
v1_router = APIRouter(prefix="/v1")
v2_router = APIRouter(prefix="/v2")

@v1_router.get("/items/")
async def list_items_v1(): ...  # Old format

@v2_router.get("/items/")
async def list_items_v2(): ...  # New format

app.include_router(v1_router)
app.include_router(v2_router)
•

14. Testing

FastAPI applications are tested using TestClient (synchronous, built on Starlette's test utilities) or httpx.AsyncClient (for async endpoints), with app.dependency_overrides to swap real dependencies for mocks. A thorough test suite covers happy paths, validation errors (422), authentication flows, and database interactions with isolated test databases.

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import pytest

client = TestClient(app)

def test_root():
    response = client.get("/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"message": "Hello, World!"}

def test_create_item():
    response = client.post("/items/", json={"name": "Widget", "price": 9.99})
    assert response.status_code == 201
    assert response.json()["name"] == "Widget"

def test_validation_error():
    response = client.post("/items/", json={"name": "", "price": -1})
    assert response.status_code == 422  # Validation error

# ── Async testing ────────────────────────────────────────
from httpx import AsyncClient, ASGITransport

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_async():
    transport = ASGITransport(app=app)
    async with AsyncClient(transport=transport, base_url="http://test") as ac:
        response = await ac.get("/")
        assert response.status_code == 200

# ── Test with DB override ───────────────────────────────
def override_get_db():
    db = TestingSessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
•

15. Observability & Health Checks

Health check endpoints (/health, /health/ready) let load balancers and orchestrators verify that your service and its dependencies are operational, while structured logging and distributed tracing provide visibility into request flows and performance. These are non-negotiable for any production deployment behind Kubernetes or a load balancer.

# ── Health checks ────────────────────────────────────────
@app.get("/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "healthy"}

@app.get("/health/ready")
async def readiness():
    try:
        db.execute("SELECT 1")
        return {"status": "ready", "db": "connected"}
    except Exception:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="DB unavailable")

# ── Structured logging ──────────────────────────────────
import structlog
logger = structlog.get_logger()

@app.middleware("http")
async def log_requests(request: Request, call_next):
    logger.info("request_start", method=request.method, url=str(request.url))
    response = await call_next(request)
    logger.info("request_end", status=response.status_code)
    return response
•

16. Deployment

Deploying FastAPI in production typically involves running Uvicorn workers behind Gunicorn as a process manager, packaged in a minimal Docker image, and fronted by a reverse proxy (Nginx or Traefik) for HTTPS termination and load balancing. Following a deployment checklist — environment-based config, health checks, structured logging, and graceful shutdown — ensures reliability at scale.

# Dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000", "--workers", "4"]
DEPLOYMENT CHECKLIST:
  ✅ Use Gunicorn + Uvicorn workers (gunicorn -w 4 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker)
  ✅ Set workers = 2 × CPU cores + 1
  ✅ Use --proxy-headers behind a reverse proxy
  ✅ Environment variables for config (not hardcoded)
  ✅ Docker multi-stage build (smaller image)
  ✅ Health check endpoint for K8s/load balancer
  ✅ HTTPS termination at reverse proxy (nginx/traefik)
  ✅ Rate limiting at API gateway or application level
  ✅ Structured JSON logging
  ✅ Graceful shutdown handling
•

17. Interview Deep Dive

GunicornDockerReverse proxyKubernetesCeleryWebSocket

Q1: Why FastAPI over Flask/Django?

A: FastAPI: async-native (ASGI), auto-validation via Pydantic, auto-generated OpenAPI docs, type hints everywhere, fastest Python framework. Flask: simpler, synchronous (WSGI), no built-in validation, larger ecosystem. Django: batteries-included (ORM, admin, auth), heavier, synchronous by default (Django 4.1+ added async). Choose FastAPI for: APIs, microservices, ML model serving. Django for: full web apps with admin panel. Flask for: simple projects, existing codebase.

Q2: Explain dependency injection in FastAPI.

A: FastAPI's DI system lets you declare function dependencies via Depends(). Dependencies can be functions or classes, can yield (for setup/teardown like DB sessions), can be nested (dependency depends on another dependency), and are cached per-request. Benefits: separation of concerns, testability (override dependencies in tests), reusability. Example: get_db dependency provides a DB session, get_current_user uses OAuth2 token → both injectable via Depends().

Q3: How do you handle authentication in FastAPI?

A: FastAPI provides OAuth2PasswordBearer (token URL + auto Swagger UI integration). Flow: (1) User POSTs credentials to /token. (2) Server validates, returns JWT. (3) Subsequent requests include Authorization: Bearer <token>. (4) get_current_user dependency decodes JWT, returns user. For API keys: use APIKeyHeader. For OAuth2 with scopes: use Security() with SecurityScopes. Always hash passwords (bcrypt via passlib), use short-lived tokens + refresh tokens in production.

Q4: How do you serve an ML model with FastAPI?

A: (1) Load model at startup (not per-request): @app.on_event("startup") or lifespan. (2) Create Pydantic schemas for input/output validation. (3) Async endpoint or background task for inference. (4) Streaming response (SSE) for LLM serving. (5) Health check endpoint. (6) Rate limiting to prevent overload. (7) Batch inference endpoint for throughput. Key: Load model once, serve many. Use uvicorn --workers 4 for parallelism. For GPU models, use a single worker with async or queue (Celery/Redis).

Q5: How do you test a FastAPI application?

A: Use TestClient (sync) or httpx.AsyncClient (async). Test strategy: (1) Unit test business logic directly. (2) Integration test API endpoints with TestClient. (3) Override dependencies (app.dependency_overrides) to mock DB, auth, external services. (4) Use test database (SQLite in-memory or test PostgreSQL). (5) Test validation errors (422 responses). (6) Test auth flows (happy path + unauthorized). (7) Pytest fixtures for reusable setup.

Q6: How do you deploy FastAPI in production?

A: (1) Gunicorn with Uvicorn workers: gunicorn -w 4 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker main:app. (2) Docker: Multi-stage build, non-root user, health check. (3) Reverse proxy: Nginx or Traefik for HTTPS, load balancing. (4) Kubernetes: Deployment + Service + HPA for auto-scaling. (5) Workers = 2 × CPU cores + 1. (6) Environment variables for config. (7) Structured JSON logging. (8) Prometheus metrics for monitoring.

Q7: What is the difference between BackgroundTasks and Celery?

A: BackgroundTasks: Built-in, runs in the same process after response is sent. Good for: quick tasks (sending emails, logging). Limitations: no retries, no task queue, lost on crash. Celery: Distributed task queue with Redis/RabbitMQ broker. Good for: long-running tasks, retries, scheduled tasks, multi-worker. Choose BackgroundTasks for simple, short tasks. Choose Celery/Redis Queue when you need reliability, retries, or heavy processing.

Q8: How do you implement real-time streaming in FastAPI?

A: Two approaches: (1) WebSocket: Bidirectional, persistent connection. Use for: chat, real-time updates. @app.websocket("/ws") with accept(), receive_text(), send_text(). (2) SSE (Server-Sent Events): Server-to-client only, uses StreamingResponse with text/event-stream. Use for: LLM streaming, live feeds. Format: data: {chunk}\n\n. SSE is simpler and works over HTTP/1.1; WebSocket is more powerful but more complex.

PUT vs PATCH

Both are used to update resources, but they behave differently.

•

PUT (Full Update)

PUT replaces the entire resource.

PUT /users/1

Request:

{
  "name": "John",
  "age": 30
}

If the user originally had:

{
  "name": "John",
  "age": 25,
  "city": "Delhi"
}

After PUT:

{
  "name": "John",
  "age": 30
}

The entire resource is replaced.

Characteristics

  • Full update
  • Idempotent
  • Missing fields may be removed
•

PATCH (Partial Update)

PATCH modifies only specified fields.

PATCH /users/1

Request:

{
  "age": 30
}

Result:

{
  "name": "John",
  "age": 30,
  "city": "Delhi"
}

Only provided fields are updated.

Characteristics

  • Partial update
  • Idempotent (usually)
  • More efficient for large objects
•

Interview Answer

PUT = Replace entire resource.

PATCH = Update only specific fields.

URL vs URI
•

URI (Uniform Resource Identifier)

A URI identifies a resource.

Examples:

/user/123
products/1
urn:isbn:123456789
•

URL (Uniform Resource Locator)

A URL is a type of URI that tells where and how to access a resource.

Example:

https://api.company.com/users/123

Components:

https://api.company.com/users/123
│      │              │
│      │              └─ Path
│      └─ Domain
└─ Protocol
•

Relationship

URI
│
├── URL
└── URN

Every URL is a URI.

Not every URI is a URL.

•

Interview Answer

URL tells location + access method.

URI only identifies the resource.

HTTP 401 vs 403

These are among the most commonly asked interview questions.

•

401 Unauthorized

Authentication is missing or invalid.

Example:

GET /users
Authorization: Missing

Response:

401 Unauthorized

Meaning:

Who are you?
Please authenticate first.

Examples:

  • Missing JWT token
  • Expired token
  • Invalid API key
•

403 Forbidden

Authentication succeeded but access is denied.

Example:

GET /admin
Authorization: Valid User Token

Response:

403 Forbidden

Meaning:

I know who you are.
But you don't have permission.

Examples:

  • User trying to access admin APIs
  • Insufficient privileges
  • Access restricted by policy
•

Easy Memory Trick

401:

Not Logged In

403:

Logged In
But Not Allowed
Rate Limiting

Rate limiting restricts the number of requests a client can make within a given time period.

Example:

100 requests/minute

If exceeded:

429 Too Many Requests
•

Why Use Rate Limiting?

  • Prevent abuse
  • Prevent brute-force attacks
  • Protect backend services
  • Reduce infrastructure costs
  • Ensure fairness
•

Common Algorithms

Fixed Window

100 requests/minute

Simple but can cause spikes.

Sliding Window

Tracks requests continuously.

More accurate.

Token Bucket

Bucket contains tokens.

Each request consumes one token.

Tokens refill over time.

Most commonly used.

Leaky Bucket

Requests leave the bucket at a fixed rate.

Smooths traffic spikes.

•

FastAPI Example

from slowapi import Limiter
from slowapi.util import get_remote_address

limiter = Limiter(
    key_func=get_remote_address
)

@app.get("/users")
@limiter.limit("100/minute")
async def users():
    return {"status": "ok"}
API Throttling

Throttling controls request processing speed when traffic becomes excessive.

Instead of completely blocking traffic, the system slows it down.

•

Example

Suppose:

Limit = 100 requests/minute

User sends:

1000 requests/minute

System may:

  • Delay requests
  • Queue requests
  • Reject excess requests
•

Rate Limiting vs Throttling

PurposeEnforce request quotaControl traffic speed
ActionReject requestsSlow requests
Response429 Too Many RequestsDelayed processing
GoalAbuse preventionTraffic management

FastAPI Production Guide

Performance Optimization
•

1. Connection Pooling

from sqlalchemy.pool import QueuePool
from sqlalchemy import create_engine

engine = create_engine(
    "postgresql://user:password@localhost/db",
    poolclass=QueuePool,
    pool_size=20,
    max_overflow=40,
    pool_recycle=3600,  # Recycle connections every hour
    pool_pre_ping=True,  # Verify connection before using
)
•

2. Query Optimization

from fastapi import FastAPI
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, joinedload

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/users/{user_id}")
async def get_user_with_posts(user_id: int, db: Session):
    # Bad: N+1 queries
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()
    posts = db.query(Post).filter(Post.user_id == user_id).all()
    
    # Good: Single query with join
    user = db.query(User).options(
        joinedload(User.posts)
    ).filter(User.id == user_id).first()
    
    return user
•

3. Pagination

from fastapi import Query

@app.get("/posts")
async def list_posts(
    skip: int = Query(0, ge=0),
    limit: int = Query(10, ge=1, le=100),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db)
):
    posts = db.query(Post).offset(skip).limit(limit).all()
    return posts

4. Caching with Redis

import redis
from typing import Optional
import json

redis_client = redis.Redis(host='localhost', port=6379, db=0)

@app.get("/cached-data/{key}")
async def get_cached_data(key: str):
    # Try cache first
    cached = redis_client.get(key)
    if cached:
        return json.loads(cached)
    
    # Fetch and cache
    data = {"data": "expensive computation"}
    redis_client.setex(key, 3600, json.dumps(data))
    return data

Security Best Practices
•

1. Authentication & Authorization

from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from jose import JWTError, jwt
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from pydantic import BaseModel

SECRET_KEY = "your-secret-key-keep-it-safe"
ALGORITHM = "HS256"

class Token(BaseModel):
    access_token: str
    token_type: str

def create_access_token(data: dict):
    to_encode = data.copy()
    expire = datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(hours=24)
    to_encode.update({"exp": expire})
    encoded_jwt = jwt.encode(to_encode, SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM)
    return encoded_jwt

async def get_current_user(token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme)):
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM])
        username: str = payload.get("sub")
        if username is None:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=401)
    except JWTError:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401)
    return username

@app.get("/protected")
async def protected_route(current_user: str = Depends(get_current_user)):
    return {"user": current_user}
•

2. Password Hashing

from passlib.context import CryptContext

pwd_context = CryptContext(schemes=["bcrypt"], deprecated="auto")

def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    return pwd_context.hash(password)

def verify_password(plain_password: str, hashed_password: str) -> bool:
    return pwd_context.verify(plain_password, hashed_password)

@app.post("/register")
async def register(username: str, password: str, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    hashed = hash_password(password)
    user = User(username=username, hashed_password=hashed)
    db.add(user)
    db.commit()
    return {"status": "registered"}

Database Optimization
•

1. Indexing Strategy

When to IndexAvoid Indexing
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Index
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base

Base = declarative_base()

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    email = Column(String, unique=True, index=True)
    username = Column(String, index=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, index=True)
    
    # Composite index
    __table_args__ = (
        Index('idx_email_username', 'email', 'username'),
    )

# Migration with Alembic:
# op.create_index('idx_email', 'users', ['email'])

When to Index: - Columns used in WHERE clauses - Foreign key columns - Columns used in ORDER BY/GROUP BY - High cardinality columns

Avoid Indexing: - Low cardinality columns (boolean, status) - Columns with frequent updates - Small tables (< 1000 rows)

•

2. Query Optimization

from sqlalchemy import func

# Bad: Retrieve all and filter in Python
users = db.query(User).all()
active_users = [u for u in users if u.is_active]

# Good: Filter in database
active_users = db.query(User).filter(User.is_active == True).all()

# Aggregation
user_count = db.query(func.count(User.id)).scalar()

# GROUP BY
stats = db.query(User.status, func.count(User.id)).group_by(User.status).all()
•

3. Connection Management

from contextlib import contextmanager
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=engine)

@contextmanager
def get_session():
    session = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield session
    finally:
        session.close()

# Usage
with get_session() as session:
    user = session.query(User).first()

2. Health Checks

from fastapi import FastAPI
from sqlalchemy import text

@app.get("/health")
async def health_check(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    # Check database
    try:
        db.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
        db_status = "healthy"
    except Exception:
        db_status = "unhealthy"
    
    # Check redis
    try:
        redis_client.ping()
        redis_status = "healthy"
    except Exception:
        redis_status = "unhealthy"
    
    return {
        "status": "healthy" if all(s == "healthy" for s in [db_status, redis_status]) else "unhealthy",
        "database": db_status,
        "redis": redis_status,
    }

1. Custom Exception Handlers

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

class CustomException(Exception):

3. Pagination & Filtering

from pydantic import BaseModel

class QueryParams(BaseModel):
    skip: int = 0
    limit: int = 10
    search: str = ""
    sort_by: str = "created_at"

@app.get("/posts")
async def list_posts(params: QueryParams = Depends()):
    query = db.query(Post)
    
    if params.search:
        query = query.filter(Post.title.ilike(f"%{params.search}%"))
    
    query = query.order_by(params.sort_by)
    posts = query.offset(params.skip).limit(params.limit).all()
    
    return posts

FastAPI Production Patterns37 sections

FastAPI — End-to-End Notes & Interview Guide

1. Introduction

FastAPI is a modern, high-performance Python web framework for building APIs.

FeatureDetail
Built onStarlette (ASGI) + Pydantic (data validation)
Python version3.7+ (3.10+ recommended)
PerformanceOn par with Node.js / Go (thanks to async + Uvicorn)
Auto docsSwagger UI (/docs) & ReDoc (/redoc) generated automatically
Type hintsUses Python type hints for validation, serialization, and docs

Why FastAPI over Flask / Django REST?

AspectFlaskDjango RESTFastAPI
Async nativeNo (needs hacks)NoYes
Auto validationNoSerializersPydantic
Auto docsNo (Swagger via ext)Yes (DRF)Yes (OpenAPI)
PerformanceModerateModerateVery High
Learning curveLowMediumLow-Medium
2. Installation & Project Setup

Install

pip install fastapi uvicorn[standard]

Minimal App

# main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/")
def read_root():
    return {"message": "Hello, FastAPI!"}

Run

uvicorn main:app --reload
  • main → file name
  • app → FastAPI instance
  • --reload → auto-reload on code change (dev only)

Access

URLPurpose
http://127.0.0.1:8000API root
http://127.0.0.1:8000/docsSwagger UI
http://127.0.0.1:8000/redocReDoc
3. Core Concepts

3.1 ASGI vs WSGI

WSGI (Flask/Django)          ASGI (FastAPI)
─────────────────            ─────────────
Synchronous only             Sync + Async
One request at a time        Concurrent requests
Uses Gunicorn                Uses Uvicorn / Hypercorn

3.2 Async / Await

import asyncio
import httpx

# Sync endpoint
@app.get("/sync")
def sync_endpoint():
    return {"msg": "I am synchronous"}

# Async endpoint
@app.get("/async")
async def async_endpoint():
    async with httpx.AsyncClient() as client:
        resp = await client.get("https://api.example.com/data")
    return resp.json()

Rule of thumb: Use async def when doing I/O-bound work (DB queries, HTTP calls). Use def for CPU-bound work — FastAPI will run it in a thread pool automatically.

3.3 Path Operations (HTTP Methods)

@app.get("/items")          # Read
@app.post("/items")         # Create
@app.put("/items/{id}")     # Full Update
@app.patch("/items/{id}")   # Partial Update
@app.delete("/items/{id}")  # Delete
4. Path & Query Parameters

4.1 Path Parameters

@app.get("/users/{user_id}")
def get_user(user_id: int):
    return {"user_id": user_id}
  • FastAPI auto-validates: /users/abc → 422 error
  • /users/42 → {"user_id": 42}

4.2 Path Parameter with Enum

from enum import Enum

class ModelName(str, Enum):
    alexnet = "alexnet"
    resnet = "resnet"
    lenet = "lenet"

@app.get("/models/{model_name}")
def get_model(model_name: ModelName):
    return {"model": model_name.value}

4.3 Query Parameters

# GET /items?skip=0&limit=10
@app.get("/items")
def read_items(skip: int = 0, limit: int = 10):
    return {"skip": skip, "limit": limit}

4.4 Optional Query Parameters

from typing import Optional

@app.get("/items/{item_id}")
def read_item(item_id: int, q: Optional[str] = None):
    result = {"item_id": item_id}
    if q:
        result["q"] = q
    return result

4.5 Query Parameter Validation

from fastapi import Query

@app.get("/items")
def read_items(
    q: str = Query(
        default=None,
        min_length=3,
        max_length=50,
        regex="^fixedquery$",
        title="Query string",
        description="Query string for searching items",
    )
):
    return {"q": q}
5. Request Body & Pydantic Models

5.1 Basic Pydantic Model

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Optional

class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str
    description: Optional[str] = None
    price: float = Field(..., gt=0, description="Price must be greater than 0")
    tax: Optional[float] = None

@app.post("/items")
def create_item(item: Item):
    total = item.price + (item.tax or 0)
    return {"name": item.name, "total_price": total}

5.2 Nested Models

class Address(BaseModel):
    street: str
    city: str
    zip_code: str

class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    age: int
    addresses: list[Address]

@app.post("/users")
def create_user(user: User):
    return user

5.3 Pydantic Validators

from pydantic import BaseModel, validator, EmailStr

class UserCreate(BaseModel):
    username: str
    email: EmailStr
    password: str
    confirm_password: str

    @validator("username")
    def username_must_be_alphanumeric(cls, v):
        assert v.isalnum(), "Username must be alphanumeric"
        return v

    @validator("confirm_password")
    def passwords_match(cls, v, values):
        if "password" in values and v != values["password"]:
            raise ValueError("Passwords do not match")
        return v

5.4 Body + Path + Query Together

@app.put("/items/{item_id}")
def update_item(
    item_id: int,                    # path param
    item: Item,                      # request body
    q: Optional[str] = None,         # query param
    importance: int = Body(default=1) # extra body field
):
    return {"item_id": item_id, "item": item, "q": q, "importance": importance}

@app.post("/items", response_model=ItemOut, status_code=201)

8. Dependency Injection

8.1 Function-based Dependency

from fastapi import Depends

def common_parameters(skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    return {"skip": skip, "limit": limit}

@app.get("/items")
def read_items(commons: dict = Depends(common_parameters)):
    return commons

@app.get("/users")
def read_users(commons: dict = Depends(common_parameters)):
    return commons

8.2 Class-based Dependency

class Pagination:
    def __init__(self, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 10):
        self.skip = skip
        self.limit = limit

@app.get("/items")
def list_items(pagination: Pagination = Depends()):
    return {"skip": pagination.skip, "limit": pagination.limit}

8.3 Sub-dependencies (Chained)

def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

def get_current_user(db=Depends(get_db), token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme)):
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.token == token).first()
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401)
    return user

@app.get("/me")
def read_me(user=Depends(get_current_user)):
    return user

8.4 Global Dependencies

app = FastAPI(dependencies=[Depends(verify_api_key)])
9. Middleware

9.1 Custom Middleware

import time
from fastapi import Request

@app.middleware("http")
async def add_process_time_header(request: Request, call_next):
    start = time.time()
    response = await call_next(request)
    process_time = time.time() - start
    response.headers["X-Process-Time"] = str(process_time)
    return response

9.2 Trusted Host Middleware

from starlette.middleware.trustedhost import TrustedHostMiddleware

app.add_middleware(TrustedHostMiddleware, allowed_hosts=["example.com", "*.example.com"])

9.3 GZip Middleware

from starlette.middleware.gzip import GZipMiddleware

app.add_middleware(GZipMiddleware, minimum_size=1000)
10. Authentication & Authorization (OAuth2 / JWT)

10.1 OAuth2 Password Flow with JWT

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Optional

from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from fastapi.security import OAuth2PasswordBearer, OAuth2PasswordRequestForm
from jose import JWTError, jwt
from passlib.context import CryptContext
from pydantic import BaseModel

# --- Config ---
SECRET_KEY = "your-secret-key"
ALGORITHM = "HS256"
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES = 30

# --- Security Utils ---
pwd_context = CryptContext(schemes=["bcrypt"], deprecated="auto")
oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="token")

# --- Models ---
class Token(BaseModel):
    access_token: str
    token_type: str

class TokenData(BaseModel):
    username: Optional[str] = None

class UserInDB(BaseModel):
    username: str
    hashed_password: str

# --- Helpers ---
def verify_password(plain, hashed):
    return pwd_context.verify(plain, hashed)

def get_password_hash(password):
    return pwd_context.hash(password)

def create_access_token(data: dict, expires_delta: Optional[timedelta] = None):
    to_encode = data.copy()
    expire = datetime.utcnow() + (expires_delta or timedelta(minutes=15))
    to_encode.update({"exp": expire})
    return jwt.encode(to_encode, SECRET_KEY, algorithm=ALGORITHM)

# --- Dependency ---
async def get_current_user(token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme)):
    credentials_exception = HTTPException(
        status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
        detail="Could not validate credentials",
        headers={"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"},
    )
    try:
        payload = jwt.decode(token, SECRET_KEY, algorithms=[ALGORITHM])
        username: str = payload.get("sub")
        if username is None:
            raise credentials_exception
    except JWTError:
        raise credentials_exception
    # In real app: fetch user from DB
    return {"username": username}

# --- Endpoints ---
@app.post("/token", response_model=Token)
async def login(form_data: OAuth2PasswordRequestForm = Depends()):
    # In real app: verify against DB
    if form_data.username != "admin" or form_data.password != "secret":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Incorrect credentials")
    access_token = create_access_token(
        data={"sub": form_data.username},
        expires_delta=timedelta(minutes=ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES),
    )
    return {"access_token": access_token, "token_type": "bearer"}

@app.get("/users/me")
async def read_users_me(current_user=Depends(get_current_user)):
    return current_user

10.2 Role-Based Access

from enum import Enum

class Role(str, Enum):
    admin = "admin"
    user = "user"

def require_role(required: Role):
    def role_checker(current_user=Depends(get_current_user)):
        if current_user.get("role") != required:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Insufficient permissions")
        return current_user
    return role_checker

@app.get("/admin-dashboard")
def admin_dashboard(user=Depends(require_role(Role.admin))):
    return {"msg": "Welcome, admin!"}
11. Database Integration (SQLAlchemy / async)

11.1 Sync SQLAlchemy Setup

# database.py
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URL = "sqlite:///./app.db"

engine = create_engine(
    SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URL, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}
)
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
Base = declarative_base()
# models.py
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Float
from database import Base

class ItemDB(Base):
    __tablename__ = "items"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True)
    name = Column(String, index=True)
    price = Column(Float)
    description = Column(String, nullable=True)
# schemas.py
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Optional

class ItemCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str
    price: float
    description: Optional[str] = None

class ItemResponse(ItemCreate):
    id: int

    class Config:
        from_attributes = True   # Pydantic v2 (formerly orm_mode = True)
# crud.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from models import ItemDB
from schemas import ItemCreate

def create_item(db: Session, item: ItemCreate):
    db_item = ItemDB(**item.model_dump())
    db.add(db_item)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(db_item)
    return db_item

def get_items(db: Session, skip: int = 0, limit: int = 100):
    return db.query(ItemDB).offset(skip).limit(limit).all()

def get_item(db: Session, item_id: int):
    return db.query(ItemDB).filter(ItemDB.id == item_id).first()
# main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from database import SessionLocal, engine, Base
from schemas import ItemCreate, ItemResponse
import crud

Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

app = FastAPI()

def get_db():
    db = SessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

@app.post("/items", response_model=ItemResponse, status_code=201)
def create_item(item: ItemCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return crud.create_item(db, item)

@app.get("/items", response_model=list[ItemResponse])
def list_items(skip: int = 0, limit: int = 10, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    return crud.get_items(db, skip, limit)

@app.get("/items/{item_id}", response_model=ItemResponse)
def read_item(item_id: int, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    db_item = crud.get_item(db, item_id)
    if not db_item:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
    return db_item

11.2 Async SQLAlchemy (with asyncpg)

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import create_async_engine, AsyncSession
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker

DATABASE_URL = "postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@localhost/dbname"

engine = create_async_engine(DATABASE_URL, echo=True)
async_session = sessionmaker(engine, class_=AsyncSession, expire_on_commit=False)

async def get_db():
    async with async_session() as session:
        yield session

@app.get("/items")
async def list_items(db: AsyncSession = Depends(get_db)):
    result = await db.execute(select(ItemDB))
    return result.scalars().all()

12.1 Simple Background Task

from fastapi import BackgroundTasks

def write_log(message: str):
    with open("log.txt", "a") as f:
        f.write(f"{message}\n")

@app.post("/send-notification")
async def send_notification(
    email: str,
    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
):

12.2 Background Task in Dependency

def log_dependency(background_tasks: BackgroundTasks, q: Optional[str] = None):
    if q:
        background_tasks.add_task(write_log, f"Query: {q}")
    return q

@app.get("/items")
def read_items(query=Depends(log_dependency)):
    return {"query": query}

For heavy/long-running jobs, use Celery or ARQ instead of BackgroundTasks.

13. WebSockets
from fastapi import WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect

class ConnectionManager:
    def __init__(self):
        self.active_connections: list[WebSocket] = []

    async def connect(self, websocket: WebSocket):
        await websocket.accept()
        self.active_connections.append(websocket)

    def disconnect(self, websocket: WebSocket):
        self.active_connections.remove(websocket)

    async def broadcast(self, message: str):
        for conn in self.active_connections:
            await conn.send_text(message)

manager = ConnectionManager()

@app.websocket("/ws/{client_id}")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket, client_id: int):
    await manager.connect(websocket)
    try:
        while True:
            data = await websocket.receive_text()
            await manager.broadcast(f"Client #{client_id}: {data}")
    except WebSocketDisconnect:
        manager.disconnect(websocket)
        await manager.broadcast(f"Client #{client_id} left the chat")

19. Rate Limiting

19.1 What Is Rate Limiting?

Rate limiting controls how many requests a client can make within a time window. It protects your API from: - Abuse / DDoS attacks - Resource exhaustion (CPU, DB connections) - Cost control (third-party API calls) - Fair usage across clients

Client sends 100 requests in 1 second
         ↓
    Rate Limiter
         ↓
  First 10 → ✅ 200 OK
  Next 90  → ❌ 429 Too Many Requests

19.2 Common Algorithms

AlgorithmHow It WorksProsCons
Fixed WindowCount reqs in fixed time slots (e.g., per minute)SimpleBurst at window edges
Sliding WindowRolling window, smooth countingNo edge burstSlightly complex
Token BucketTokens refill at fixed rate; each req costs 1 tokenAllows burstsMemory per client
Leaky BucketRequests queue and process at fixed rateSmooth outputDelays under load

19.3 Rate Limiting with slowapi (Production-Ready)

pip install slowapi
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from slowapi import Limiter, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler
from slowapi.util import get_remote_address
from slowapi.errors import RateLimitExceeded

# Create limiter using client IP as key
limiter = Limiter(key_func=get_remote_address)

app = FastAPI()
app.state.limiter = limiter
app.add_exception_handler(RateLimitExceeded, _rate_limit_exceeded_handler)

# --- Global rate limit ---
@app.get("/")
@limiter.limit("5/minute")  # 5 requests per minute per IP
async def homepage(request: Request):
    return {"message": "Welcome!"}

# --- Different limits per endpoint ---
@app.get("/search")
@limiter.limit("10/minute")
async def search(request: Request, q: str = ""):
    return {"query": q, "results": []}

@app.post("/login")
@limiter.limit("3/minute")  # Strict limit on login attempts
async def login(request: Request):
    return {"token": "abc123"}

@app.get("/premium")
@limiter.limit("100/minute")  # Higher limit for premium
async def premium_endpoint(request: Request):
    return {"data": "premium content"}

19.4 Custom Rate Limiter (From Scratch)

import time
from collections import defaultdict
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()

class RateLimiter:
    """Simple in-memory sliding window rate limiter."""
    def __init__(self, max_requests: int, window_seconds: int):
        self.max_requests = max_requests
        self.window_seconds = window_seconds
        self.requests: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)
    
    def is_allowed(self, client_id: str) -> bool:
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - self.window_seconds
        
        # Remove expired timestamps
        self.requests[client_id] = [
            ts for ts in self.requests[client_id] if ts > window_start
        ]
        
        if len(self.requests[client_id]) >= self.max_requests:
            return False
        
        self.requests[client_id].append(now)
        return True
    
    def remaining(self, client_id: str) -> int:
        now = time.time()
        window_start = now - self.window_seconds
        active = [ts for ts in self.requests[client_id] if ts > window_start]
        return max(0, self.max_requests - len(active))

# 10 requests per 60 seconds
rate_limiter = RateLimiter(max_requests=10, window_seconds=60)

@app.middleware("http")
async def rate_limit_middleware(request: Request, call_next):
    client_ip = request.client.host
    
    if not rate_limiter.is_allowed(client_ip):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=429,
            detail="Rate limit exceeded. Try again later.",
            headers={"Retry-After": "60"},
        )
    
    response = await call_next(request)
    # Add rate limit headers
    response.headers["X-RateLimit-Limit"] = str(rate_limiter.max_requests)
    response.headers["X-RateLimit-Remaining"] = str(
        rate_limiter.remaining(client_ip)
    )
    return response

@app.get("/items")
def get_items():
    return {"items": ["item1", "item2", "item3"]}

@app.get("/users")
def get_users():
    return {"users": ["alice", "bob"]}

19.5 Redis-Based Rate Limiter (Distributed)

import redis.asyncio as redis
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()
redis_client = redis.from_url("redis://localhost:6379")

async def check_rate_limit(
    client_id: str, max_requests: int = 100, window: int = 60
) -> bool:
    key = f"rate_limit:{client_id}"
    current = await redis_client.get(key)
    
    if current and int(current) >= max_requests:
        return False
    
    pipe = redis_client.pipeline()
    pipe.incr(key)
    pipe.expire(key, window)  # Auto-expire after window
    await pipe.execute()
    return True

@app.middleware("http")
async def rate_limit_middleware(request: Request, call_next):
    client_ip = request.client.host
    if not await check_rate_limit(client_ip, max_requests=100, window=60):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=429, detail="Rate limit exceeded")
    return await call_next(request)
20. Pagination

20.1 Why Pagination?

Without pagination:                 With pagination:
──────────────────                  ─────────────────
GET /users → 1,000,000 rows         GET /users?page=1&size=20 → 20 rows
Slow response (10+ seconds)         Fast response (~50ms)
High memory usage                   Low memory usage
Browser/client may crash             Smooth user experience
DB under heavy load                  DB handles easily

20.2 Pagination Strategies

StrategyURL ExampleProsCons
Offset-based?page=3&size=20Simple, supports jumping to any pageSlow for large offsets, inconsistent on inserts
Cursor-based?cursor=abc123&size=20Consistent, fast for all pagesCan't jump to arbitrary page
Keyset?after_id=100&size=20Very fast (uses index)Only works with sortable unique keys

20.3 Offset-Based Pagination (Complete Example)

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, Depends
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Optional, Generic, TypeVar, List
import math

app = FastAPI()

# --- Fake Database ---
fake_users_db = [
    {"id": i, "name": f"User_{i}", "email": f"user{i}@example.com"}
    for i in range(1, 201)  # 200 users
]

# --- Schemas ---
class UserOut(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    email: str

class PaginationMeta(BaseModel):
    page: int
    size: int
    total_items: int
    total_pages: int
    has_next: bool
    has_prev: bool

class PaginatedResponse(BaseModel):
    data: list[UserOut]
    meta: PaginationMeta

# --- Dependency for pagination params ---
class PaginationParams:
    def __init__(
        self,
        page: int = Query(1, ge=1, description="Page number"),
        size: int = Query(20, ge=1, le=100, description="Items per page"),
    ):
        self.page = page
        self.size = size
        self.offset = (page - 1) * size

# --- Endpoint ---
@app.get("/users", response_model=PaginatedResponse)
def list_users(pagination: PaginationParams = Depends()):
    # Simulate DB query with OFFSET and LIMIT
    total = len(fake_users_db)
    items = fake_users_db[pagination.offset : pagination.offset + pagination.size]
    total_pages = math.ceil(total / pagination.size)
    
    return PaginatedResponse(
        data=items,
        meta=PaginationMeta(
            page=pagination.page,
            size=pagination.size,
            total_items=total,
            total_pages=total_pages,
            has_next=pagination.page < total_pages,
            has_prev=pagination.page > 1,
        ),
    )

    {"id": 7, "name": "User_7", "email": "user7@example.com"},
    {"id": 8, "name": "User_8", "email": "user8@example.com"},
    {"id": 9, "name": "User_9", "email": "user9@example.com"},
